source.crs: EPSG:4258 (ETRS89, lat/lon), transformed to the map's Lambert azimuthal equal-area frame

SE.reason: Sweden's register (Myndigheten för civilt försvar) covers about 64,000 shelters, which in war are open to anyone nearby; it is published as a map, but no openly licensed dataset with redistribution terms was found. The Swedish and Norwegian classifications also differ (Sweden has no separate 'public' class), so the two would not be comparable.

DK.reason: Denmark has no published national dataset of public shelter locations; a national inspection of public shelters (betondækningsgrave) ran in 2025–26, and the results have not been released as open data.

meaning.places: Registered places: the capacity DSB records for the shelter room. Not current availability, readiness, accessibility or guaranteed protection.
meaning.public: Public shelters are for anyone in the area. Private shelters (housing, schools, workplaces) hold most of Norway's shelter places and are not in this dataset.
meaning.absence: A municipality without a public shelter here may still have private shelters or other protection.
meaning.residents: Shelters serve the people present in an area, not only registered residents, so places are not compared with population.

rules.municipality: Point in polygon against the Kartverket 2024 municipal boundaries used by the app; records just outside a simplified outline go to the nearest municipality (≤ 1500 m), and the distance is kept.
rules.position: Each record keeps its published position. The map groups nearby shelters into one symbol at small scales; a group symbol stands at the members' mean position and says how many it holds.
